iut_type: End Product profile retest (DensoTen), test environment requirements
customer_question: Are there any PTS test items that require a special test environment, such as an anechoic chamber or shielded room? If any of our remaining Fail items need such an environment, please let us know.
question_variants: Does Bluetooth SIG require specific RF-isolated test environments for any profile test items?
Could environmental RF interference be contributing to our Fail results?
actual_issue: The customer, troubleshooting profile test failures, wanted to know whether a lack of a specialized RF-isolated test environment could be a factor in their Fail results, and whether SIG mandates such an environment for any specific test items.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG does not require PTS testing to be conducted in an anechoic chamber or shielded room — any environment is acceptable as certification evidence as long as a Pass result is obtained. That said, locations with less competing wireless interference (such as from Wi-Fi) are generally more likely to produce a Pass, so testing in a location with weaker Wi-Fi signal presence is recommended as a practical way to improve Pass likelihood, even though it isn't a formal requirement.
consultant_answer: No, SIG doesn't require an anechoic chamber or shielded room for PTS testing — any environment producing a Pass result is acceptable as certification evidence. That said, locations with less competing wireless interference (especially Wi-Fi) tend to pass more reliably, so we'd recommend testing somewhere with weaker Wi-Fi signal presence as a practical way to improve your odds, even though it's not a formal requirement.
decision_logic: Test environment requirements for PTS testing are evidence-outcome-based (any environment producing a valid Pass is acceptable) rather than environment-type-mandated, though minimizing RF interference is a practical recommendation for improving Pass likelihood.
final_recommendation: When customers ask about specialized test environment requirements, clarify that SIG's requirement is outcome-based (a valid Pass result, any environment) rather than environment-type-mandated, while still offering the practical tip of testing in a low-interference location to improve success odds.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer mistakenly believing an anechoic chamber is mandatory could incur unnecessary cost and delay seeking out specialized facilities, when standard environments with reasonable wireless interference levels are fully acceptable.
